objective: Review the four platform design skills and their shared core (commit b5d21e1 on release/0.2.1/feat/design-skills) against Part C of the 0.2.1 request.
scope: Read /home/user/holyagent-work/spec-0.2.1.md Part C in full (binding, approved as written) and /home/user/holyagent-work/research.md items 4 and 5.

Read the generated skills /home/user/holyagent-feat-design-skills/packages/integrations/claude/dist/skills/{web,mobile,desktop,tui}-design/SKILL.md, the core source packages/runtime/src/instructions/claude-5.5/design-core/core.md and docs/attributions.md there; the diff is /home/user/holyagent-work/diffs/design-skills.diff. Compare with the shape of packages/integrations/claude/vendor/frontend-design/SKILL.md.

Check each binding requirement: stack-agnostic (no framework, library, kit or API names; stack-dependent rules tell the reader to detect and map); every rule checkable on a render, behavioral rules phrased as visible symptoms, behavior checks marked for Worker.operations, taste marked as preference; lean prose, no machinery, numbers only where a platform fixes them or as overridable defaults; 80-140 lines; descriptions start 'Use when'; the shared core content matches the spec's Shared core; each skill's platform rules cover the spec's bullets (list any dropped or changed bullet and say whether the change is justified by research.md, e.g. Android compact navigation); refuse lists and capture checklists present; paraphrase, not copied text; credits complete with owner/repo or URL and license.

Apply the instruction-writing rules in /home/user/holyagent-feat-design-skills/packages/runtime/src/instructions/claude-5.5/skills/instruction-writing/SKILL.md: ambiguity, unclear triggers, contradictions between the core and a skill or between skills.
constraints: Keep working until the review is done; stop to ask only when you cannot go on. When done, stop and report; name anything unrequested instead of doing it. Read-only: change no repository files and make no git writes.
Each finding: file:line, the requirement it misses, blocking or not, smallest fix. Report in under 700 words.

result:
result: all Part C binding requirements are met or justified, with two blocking taste-marking gaps in the core (finding 1) and mobile-design (finding 2); the remaining findings do not block. I did not compare the skills' wording against the source skills, so the paraphrase requirement is partly unverified. I ran no checks and changed no files. Evidence is the four built skills, `core.md`, `docs/attributions.md` and the diff, read at b5d21e1.

**requirement-verdicts**
- Stack-agnostic: met. A search of the four built skills for framework, kit and API names found only "Nerd Font" at `tui-design/SKILL.md:75`, a font and not a framework. Each skill tells the reader to detect the stack and map the rule (`core.md:15`). The test at `design-skills.test.ts` bans the right terms.
- Checkable on a render and symptom phrasing: gap (findings 1, 2, 5). Behavior checks are marked for Worker.operations and the TUI hygiene checks are correctly routed to it.
- Lean, no machinery: met. The built skills are 100, 94, 95 and 110 lines, all within 80 to 140. The numbers are platform-fixed or tagged as defaults.
- Descriptions start "Use when": met in all four. `web-design` leads with the situation, then what it holds.
- Shared core matches the spec: met. `core.md` carries every spec bullet and has a single source, embedded by the generator with a test.
- Platform bullets: all present, with the changes below.
  - Dropped: web "8 to 10 gray shades" (`web-design:53`), justified by the no-numeric-dials rule.
  - Dropped: Android compact "(or a modal rail or drawer)" (`mobile-design:71`), justified by research item 4 ("compact windows always use a navigation bar").
  - Resolved: Android "expanded rail over drawer" [verify] is confirmed by research item 4.
  - Changed: iOS 27 [verify] became a "no remembered rule" line (finding 4).
  - Merged: the Android "fake Material" refuse list sits in the single mobile refuse list (`mobile-design:78-87`).
  - Desktop and TUI: nothing dropped.
- Refuse lists and capture checklists: met in all four. Web has all ten spec items. Desktop and TUI refuse lists are additions the spec did not list.
- Paraphrase: unverified against sources. The text reads as original, and the only close phrase is "remove one accessory" (`core.md:23`), from the credited `frontend-design`.
- Credits: met. `attributions.md:20-44` lists every source in the spec with URL and license. The unverified-license mxcl source is marked "ideas only", and clig.dev is marked CC BY-SA 4.0 and paraphrased.
- Instruction-writing rules: met apart from the contradictions and ambiguities in the findings.

**findings**
1. Blocking. `core.md:7-9, 23-24` (built at `web-design:17-19, 33-34`, and the same in the other three). These rules are taste or process and no capture can show them, but are unmarked, so `core.md:3` makes a violation "material". Examples: a plan, a refinement or redesign statement, one signature detail, remove one accessory, a gray placeholder over drawn art. This breaks the requirement to mark taste as preference and to map each rule to a material effect. Fix: tag the "one signature detail / remove one accessory" bullet and the placeholder bullet `(preference)`. Say in `core.md:3` that the direction rules are checked as a plan in the worker's report or `DESIGN.md`, not on a render.
2. Blocking. `mobile-design:64`. `(preference)` covers the whole bullet, including "every custom color has light, dark and increased-contrast variants", which is a visible accessibility rule. It would be listed and never repaired. Fix: split the bullet and keep `(preference)` only on "no in-app appearance switch" and the 7:1 aim.
3. Non-blocking, to handle in the root-integration PR. `core.md:3` is a third copy of the materiality list, next to `visual-judging` and `interface-inspection.md`. It already differs: it omits "adherence to a reference" and "responsiveness at a listed size". The spec says to align the two into one source. Fix: make one source and have the core and `visual-judging` point to it.
4. Non-blocking. `mobile-design:63`. "rely on no remembered rule" is ambiguous, and the sentence is tied to a dated Apple release. Fix: "iOS 27 guidance on scroll edges, sidebars, tab bars, menus, search and icons is not encoded here; judge those on a render of the target OS."
5. Non-blocking. `mobile-design:76`. `(preference)` also covers "Choose components by behavior". Fix: place it on the expressive-motion clause only.
6. Non-blocking. `desktop-design:93` asks for a 150% or 200% text scale on every platform, but `desktop-design:65` says macOS has no dynamic text size. Fix: "where the platform has a text scale".
7. Non-blocking. `core.md:30` assumes larger-text and high-contrast settings exist on every platform, including a terminal UI. Fix: "where the platform has them".
8. Non-blocking. `web-design:65` requires the label to be shown as a tooltip on hover and focus, but the spec only requires a label. Fix: "has an accessible label; a tooltip on hover and focus where a pointer exists".
9. Non-blocking. `web-design:46, 52, 54` use `(defaults)` and `(default)`, a marker the core does not define. `web-design:77` says "position-like transforms", which is vague. Fix: use one defined marker and write "transform and opacity".
